steps.text: Beat whipping cream in a large bowl until stiff peaks form; set aside.
Combine cream cheese, sugar, vanilla, and salt in a large bowl. Beat until smooth, then fold in whipped cream until incorporated.

raw_recipe.headline: Whipped Cream Cream Cheese Frosting
raw_recipe.description: A whipped cream cheese frosting that is delicate but creamy, making it the perfect icing on any cake. This will be your new favorite frosting.
raw_recipe.name: Whipped Cream Cream Cheese Frosting

review.reviewBody:
YUMMY YUMMY YUMMY! Thank you! A few of you have mentioned lumps in the frosting. What works for me, I warm my mixing bowl with hot water first. It is just enough warmth to "melt?" the cream cheese. Then use a chilled bowl for the Whipped cream, whip till very stiff. Maybe why some are having trouble with it being runny. Fold together and it is absolutely scrumptious!! Awesome flavor! So much lighter than a Cream Cheese frosting. It won't over power the flavor of your cake. Had many requests.
MAY I ADD A HINT TO ALL WHO HAVE HAD TROUBLE WITH THIS RECIPE BEING RUNNY! IF USING THE SAME BOWL AND BEATERS YOU MUST WHIP THE CREAM FIRST. IF THERE IS EVEN A HINT OF THE CREAM CHEESE (OILY SUBSTANCE) IN THE BOWL OR ON THE BEATERS YOU WILL NOT GET YOUR CREAM TO "WHIP" UP TO A STIFF CONSISTENCY, WHICH MEANS THE FROSTING WILL BE TOO RUNNY. YOU MUST TRY AGAIN. VERY DELICIOUS!

This was a real, real disappointment. There is NO WAY you can pipe this frosting...it is soooooooo soft and runny. I am an part time cake decorator so I am very familiar with piping frosting. I placed my bowl and beaters in the freezer and chilled my whipped cream. It was still too soft to really ice anything other than a flat sheet cake. After reading the reviews I noted that some people said use only 1 cup of whipped cream and not 1 ½ cups. Possibly that may have made it a little thicker. But my point is...the recipe as written does not work. Another reviewer suggested that this frosting can only be used on a flat, sheet type cake and I totally agree. I used this to frost a 10 inch angel food cake and it just started to drip/slide down the sides. It did not hold up well.....and that was after refrigerating and trying to chill/thicken it up. I would never make this again....stick will regular, buttercream creamcheese frosting. If you enjoy carrot cake with traditional cream cheese frosting you will not enjoy this fluffy, runny, whipped cream version.

I was nervous to make this based on the same concerns and problems coming up in many reviews and I was using this for a round devil's food cake. I always chill beaters and copper bowl.Chilled heavy cream also. Cream cheese was room temp. Debated the sugar issue:10x or granulated and chose to stick to the recipe. I beat the cream until it was almost like butter and placed it back in freezer while doing the rest. I whipped the sugar/cheese forever and there was no grainy text. When I put it together I could see that it seemed somewhat 'loose' so decided to put it back in the freezer for another 15 min. Garnished w/strawberries as seen in the pic and placed them between a papertowel to draw up the extra moisture and not leave pink 'footprints' on my frosting, or slide down the sides from wetness. The cake frosted fine although it is a very whippy frosting even after all the extra precautions. I wouldn't hesitate to just whip it up and throw it on a sheet cake but would take the extra time when doing a round cake. The taste is incredible. I love it because it is not sugary sweet but sweet enough and complimented by the cream cheese. I agree that this would make an A-1 fruit dip!!! Slathered liberally on the cake and still had about 1/2 a cottage cheese container left over so it does make plenty! I absolutely love this and would be great with almond extract on a cherry cake. This is definitely a keeper. thank you so much for such a lovely whippy non-sickening frosting!

I've played around with this recipe a bit and found the right adjustments in order to make a frosting that will hold up to the weight of a layer cake, taste like cream cheese, and still not have that dense pasty texture of most cream cheese icings. 

1 cup pasteurized heavy cream, cold
2 tbs granulated sugar
1 package Oetker (or other brand) 
 whipped cream stabilizer

16 oz cream cheese, softened
4 tbs unsalted butter, softened
1 cup powdered sugar, sifted
vanilla extract to taste 

Beat together cream cheese, butter, powdered sugar, and vanilla. 

In a separate bowl with clean beaters whip the cream, granulated sugar, and stabilizer until medium peaks form.

Add a bit of the whipped cream to the cream cheese mixture. Stir to combine. Fold in the remaining whipped cream in two additions.
I've always beaten together the sugar and cream cheese first, gradually adding the cream until blended and then beating. Works great.

This frosting is AMAZING!! Best cream cheese frosting ever! Some tips, put a metal or glass bowl and very clean beaters in the freezer for a bit before you beat the whipping cream. Once beating, it takes several minutes to firm up, be patient, it’ll get there! After beating the whipping cream, move on to the cream cheese step. Make sure your cream cheese has sat a room temp for at least a few hours, until soft to the touch. After adding the sugar and salt, make sure you beat it long enough until they are both dissolved and not gritty in the cream cheese. This is the most important step if you want to use this to decorate a cake, REFRIGERATE before using!! I have refrigerated this overnight and it worked beautifully to pipe on a cake. I have also used this immediately after making it and it was a sloppy mess so do yourself a favor and make it in advance! This is by far my favorite cream cheese frosting!

perfect. I whipped the cream way past the point of firm points: I did this as I read the frosting was runny for some people. Then I whipped the cream cheese with confectioners/powdered sugar as I misread the recipe to use white sugar. Then I folded the two together. Consistency was perfect, slightly thicker than pudding. I also used half the sugar but it was still very sweet, probably because I used powdered sugar.

This was my first time making a frosting with heavy whipping cream. It turned out wonderful and delicious! At first, I couldnt get the mixture to thicken or stiffin up at all! Then I learned everything has to be very cold. So I stuck The mixing bowl, metal mixers and frosting in the freezer for 10-15 minutes several times throughout the whipping process to keep everything cold. That is the key to this receipe! Cold! It worked and I was able to beautifully pipe!

This frosting was a hit! It was light and not too sweet. I used powdered sugar instead of granulated sugar. I was looking for a base frosting that I could add crushed Oreos to and this worked perfect. I will definitely use this recipe again.

I used 1 1/2 teaspoons of powdered milk in with the whip cream, which works to stabilize it. Whip the cream first and put in fridg. Beat room temp cream cheese with the reg. sugar, and there where no lumps. Very delicious, not to sweat or cloying like traditional frosting. It did pipe very well. Been baking and decorating cakes, including wedding cakes, for over 35 years.

Great frosting. I whipped cream using an electric hand blender with whisk attachment and blended room temp cream cheese with a hand held mixer. I chilled the whipped cream before folding in. It came out perfect. I did notice my cake was not completely cool and the frosting began to run. I let the cake cool completely and frosting spread and piped perfect. Thanks for sharing.

The flavor is amazing, so five stars it is! That said, even after following other reviewers advice on the order and chilling the bowl, it still came out somewhat liquidy. I added powdered sugar and then a little more “stiff” cream cheese, but still. I ended up spreading between layers and on top only, leaving the sides unfrosted. Added strawberries and mint leaves for garnish. It actually looked quite elegant.

I love this frosting! It’s family favorite ❤️ Not knowing how long the heavy whipping cream took to beat, I looked it up and it said to add 1 tbls of powdered sugar and 1tsp of vanilla….i added them and then found out it took about 6-8 mins of beating….so I didn’t add a tspn of vanilla to the cream cheese mixture and it turned out amazing after I was done….this is a crowd pleaser for sure!
I added 1/4 cup of strawberry purée. It was delicious
Perfect
Phenomenal!Not too sweet and insanely light AND luscious!

This recipe was delicious! I needed a quick cream cheese frosting for a strawberry cake. This was the perfect flavor and consistency. Just enough sweetness and cream cheese flavor without overpowering the strawberry flavor from the cake. Will definitely use this recipe again!

Loved the recipe-I could eat this with a spoon. It was stiff enough to hold shell borders off different sizes but too soft for flower petals. Followed the advice of whipping that cream first then cream cheese. I beat the cream cheese with the sugar and vanilla straight from the fridge then folded in the whipped cream. Balloon whisk for the cream and paddle for the cream cheese. Manually folded with a spatula. Froze a small portion to see what would happen. Mostly kept its texture but there was a little weeping after thawing. I'm going to freeze some cupcakes with the frosting piped on and see how they hold up.

This cream cheese frosting is light and doesn’t have an overpowering cream cheese taste. It is by far the best cream cheese frosting I’ve ever made. The only thing I probably wouldn’t use it on is a carrot cake just because it doesn’t have a strong cream cheese taste, but this is my first choice for all other recipes. I used it for my banana bars that I made, my husband loved it and he does not like cream cheese frosting, except this one. I followed the recipe and it was prefect. It is not a real stiff frosting, but can still be use for piping if it is not stiff enough for you you can add a little powered sugar but make sure you shift the powered sugar before adding it or it will be lumpy. Thank you for the recipe it will be used a lot.
I use this all the time I do add 3tbls of powered sugar to thicken it for piping
